summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best performers are short 'this device doesn't do what you think' videos about relatable gadgets and robots (gyro robot, clap switch, line follower, mic vs speaker), which earn the most likes, saves and shares. Generic 'How does X work?' questions about everyday places (lift door, mall door, tap, smoke detector) get little attention, and the English video and the posts with zero Instagram data are not helping.
winningPattern: Hindi Instagram Reels about a hands-on maker gadget or robot (clap switch, gyro robot, line follower, mic) with a surprising, contrarian hook that flips an assumption ('Nahi, sirf...', 'Ke bina gir jaata', 'Ulta kaam karta hai'). Titles are short, claim-style statements rather than 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' questions, and the topic is something a student could build with an Arduino. Clap switch is the strongest repeatable series, and IR sensor 'robot avoids wall' also earned the most shares.
doMore: Make 'X ke bina Y fail ho jaata' demo hooks showing the failure first, like the gyro robot
Build a series around clap switch, line follower, IR and mic, the proven maker topics
Use contrarian statement titles ('Sensor Dekhta Nahi, Sirf...') instead of 'Kaise?' questions
Post to Instagram first and cross-post to YouTube only with a stronger first 2 seconds
End with a save/share prompt such as 'Project ke liye save karo' since saves and shares signal quality
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' videos on public-place gadgets (lift, mall door, tap, street light)
Near-duplicate topics in the same week (several smoke detector, IR and tap videos) that split the audience
Publishing videos that never reach Instagram (zero IG data) or switching to English without testing it properly
nextTopics: Obstacle avoiding robot without any camera
Clap switch with a whistle or music
Line follower robot with the sensor removed
Robot balancing with and without an accelerometer
